Apple has disclosed how the new Siri artificial intelligence features operate in China. The new AI features will be powered by Alibaba's Qwen model.

Although the iPhone maker partners with Google in most countries to gain access to its Gemini model, the Chinese government requires Apple to instead partner with a local AI company...

In most countries, the new Siri AI features are powered by Google's Gemini model. These features run on Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers, or on servers provided by Google and dedicated for Apple's use, and are equipped with safeguards specifically designed for Siri AI users. These include privacy requirements comparable to those of the PCC servers, ensuring that neither Apple nor Google can access users' interactions.

However, in China, the law only permits the use of Chinese AI models. This is most likely to allow the government to monitor usage, so the same privacy safeguards will most likely not apply.

According to a Reuters report, Apple has published a guide stating that the new features will rely on Alibaba's Qwen model. The guide is intended for Mac, but the report indicates that the same model will also be used on iPhone, iPad and Vision Pro.

There is one rather obvious clue indicating that privacy safeguards will not apply in the same way: Reuters reports that Mac users will need to have their own Qwen account and must log in to that account.
